audit_findings.title: The bridge may classify operating cash as excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: At-risk bridge amount $1,094.181 million, equal to $12.99 per share and 6.75% of the $16,212 million base equity value; required operating-cash portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Required operating cash should remain inside the operating business rather than being added separately in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Our working capital needs are primarily to finance accounts receivable and inventory.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that the business is working-capital intensive, while the valuation adds all cash and short-term investments as excess. It does not establish how much cash is required, so an error is not demonstrated, but the amount exposed is large enough to materially affect value.
audit_findings.action: Determine minimum operating cash from intra-year cash balances, seasonal cash-conversion cycles, revolver usage, restricted or geographically unavailable cash, and liquidity policy; rerun the bridge adding only demonstrably surplus cash.

audit_findings.title: FY2025 interest expense may understate the forward financing cost
audit_findings.magnitude: $700.0 million August 2026 maturity, equal to $8.31 per share and 64.0% of bridge cash; six-month 2026 net finance charges annualize to $368.750 million versus $356.608 million in FY2025; refinancing-rate effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Repayment reduces bridge cash, while refinancing at a higher sustainable rate reduces equity-level OE because interest expense remains inside OE.
audit_findings.evidence: We believe that our available cash and cash equivalents balances, cash flows from operations and our existing sources of liquidity, including available capacity under our borrowing facilities, will be sufficient to enable the repayment of $700.0 million of our Senior Notes due in August 2026 and to satisfy our current and planned working capital and investment needs for the next twelve months in all geographies.
audit_findings.explanation: The maturity and the newer higher-coupon debt are demonstrated, but the ultimate repayment or refinancing treatment is unresolved. Either consuming $700 million of cash without updating the bridge or refinancing without normalizing interest could materially overstate value; repayment-related interest savings would partly offset the cash reduction.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the actual August 2026 settlement or refinancing terms and post-transaction cash and debt balances; normalize after-tax net interest for the resulting debt stack and rerun both OE and the cash bridge under one consistent funding policy.

audit_findings.title: Vendor financing may make cash and owner earnings look more durable than they are
audit_findings.magnitude: Supplier-finance obligations were $3,713.212 million at FY2025 and approximately $3.8 billion at May 31, 2026; the FY2025 increase was $539.306 million, equal to 50.1% of $1,076 million anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Extended payment terms can temporarily increase operating cash flow and cash available for the bridge; if reflected in OE working-capital assumptions, they can also inflate sustainable OE.
audit_findings.evidence: As of November 30, 2025 and 2024, the Company had $ 3.7 billion and $ 3.2 billion, respectively, in obligations outstanding under these programs included in “Accounts payable” in the Company’s Consolidated Balance Sheets and all activity related to the obligations is presented within operating activities in the Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows.
audit_findings.explanation: The large balance and FY2025 increase are demonstrated, but the record does not show how much represents abnormal term extension rather than durable trade credit. Given the increase relative to anchor OE and the total balance relative to equity value, normalization is reasonably capable of materially lowering value.
audit_findings.action: Obtain supplier-finance payment terms, comparable ordinary vendor terms, program-level rollforwards and the contribution to accounts-payable cash flow; normalize payment terms and rerun any affected working-capital component of OE and the excess-cash bridge.

audit_findings.title: Unrecorded inventory-repurchase guarantees could create a senior cash claim
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed repurchases have been insignificant, with no pending customer defaults or repossession obligations
audit_findings.mechanism: A realized guarantee loss would reduce OE if recurring or require a contingent-liability deduction in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As the Company does not have access to information regarding the amount of inventory purchased from the Company still on hand with the customer at any point in time, the Company’s repurchase obligations relating to inventory cannot be reasonably estimated.
audit_findings.explanation: The guarantee exists, but the latest filings report insignificant historical repurchases, no pending defaults and a remote likelihood of material loss. There is therefore no presently demonstrated valuation adjustment; the risk becomes valuation-relevant if customer defaults, repossessions or loss severity increase.
audit_findings.action: Monitor floor-plan exposure, customer defaults and repossession notices; obtain inventory-on-hand data and resale haircuts from financing counterparties, then rerun OE or the bridge if an expected loss or reserve becomes estimable and material.

audit_findings.title: Legacy Concentrix tax liabilities may remain with SNX
audit_findings.magnitude: Known company-wide gross unrecognized tax benefits were $17.077 million, equal to $0.20 per share and 0.11% of base equity value; Concentrix-related maximum exposure unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: An assessment not captured in normalized tax expense would reduce cash through the equity bridge or reduce OE if it represents a recurring tax burden.
audit_findings.evidence: In certain jurisdictions SYNNEX and Concentrix have joint and several liability for past income tax liabilities and accordingly, SYNNEX could be legally liable under applicable tax law for such liabilities and required to make additional tax payments.
audit_findings.explanation: Joint-and-several liability and tax-sharing obligations are demonstrated, but the filing does not identify a current Concentrix assessment or quantify the maximum exposure, including a potential loss of tax-free treatment. The disclosed company-wide uncertain-tax balance alone is not material relative to base equity value, but it does not establish the limit of the legacy exposure.
audit_findings.action: Review the Tax Matters Agreement, open pre-Separation tax years, audit notices, indemnification rights and any estimate of distribution-tax exposure; deduct an established net liability from the bridge or rerun normalized taxes if evidence shows a recurring effect.
